title: Admit composite dispatch keys only with a behavioral difference and a single field:value discriminant

facts.note: Task text mentions dispatch keys that route artifacts to trains.
Any file holding (artifact_urn[, discriminant]) -> train_id dispatch entries, whoever edits or reviews it.

values: composite (artifact_urn, discriminant) -> train_id dispatch key introduced
composite dispatch key changed (discriminant or justification)
facts.note: Needs a diff-level observer that parses dispatch entries and distinguishes composite keys from plain artifact_urn keys.

values: composite dispatch key under assessment or reported by the validator
facts.note: Covers assessing existing composite keys (review, audit, validator finding), not only new edits.

fires: A composite (artifact_urn, discriminant) -> train_id dispatch key is added to the dispatch map, by any actor in any phase.
An existing composite dispatch key's discriminant or behavioral_difference justification is changed.
A plan, review or audit assesses existing composite dispatch keys for admissibility.
A composite key is proposed whose discriminant combines two field:value pairs.
doesNotFire: A dispatch entry keyed by artifact_urn alone is added or changed.
Train or wagon documents are edited without introducing, changing or assessing any dispatch key.
A train handler is implemented without touching or assessing dispatch keys.

given: A dispatch map routes artifacts to trains, and a composite (artifact_urn, discriminant) -> train_id dispatch key exists or is proposed.
when: That composite dispatch key is introduced, changed or assessed (in a plan, acceptance, doc or review).
then: Treat the composite key as exceptional: permit it only with a behavioral_difference justification and a discriminant that is exactly one field:value.
prefer: Key dispatch by artifact_urn alone; use a composite key only when there is a behavioral difference to justify it.
State the behavioral_difference as the observable behavior that differs between the routed trains.
Write the discriminant as exactly one field:value.
avoid: Composite keys with a missing or empty behavioral_difference justification.
Discriminants that are not exactly one field:value (e.g. several fields combined, or no field:value at all).
Composite keys used for organisational convenience where train behavior is the same.
why: The dispatch map is a registry mapping an artifact to a train by default; unjustified composite keys break that default and hide why one artifact routes to different trains.
evidence: Validator implementing this convention: conventions/schema/test_dispatch_map_is_registry::test_fault_caught_by_convention (checks the dispatch map).
Each composite entry in the dispatch map has a non-empty behavioral_difference and a discriminant that is exactly one field:value.
verifier_detail: A composite key (term: composite_key) is a dispatch key of shape (artifact_urn, discriminant) -> train_id.
Flag a composite entry missing a behavioral_difference justification.
Flag a composite entry whose discriminant is not exactly one field:value.
Severity 3; disposition strict: every finding fails.
